District of Arizona Charges 374 Individuals for Immigration-Related Criminal Conduct this Week
item.description: PHOENIX, Ariz. – During the week of enforcement operations from Sep. 26 through Oct. 2, 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona brought immigration-related criminal charges against 374 individuals.

item.title: Billings man sentenced to 3 years in prison for unlawfully possessing a handgun
item.description: A Billings man who was found in his parked car unlawfully carrying a firearm was sentenced Wednesday to three years and one month in prison, followed by three years of supervised release.

item.title: Schenectady Man Sentenced to 240 Months for Distribution and Possession of Child Pornography
item.description: Gregory Magin, age 46, of Glenville, New York, was sentenced on August 4, 2026 to 240 months for distribution and possession of child pornography.First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III; Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Division Craig Tremaroli; and New York State Police (NYSP) Superintendent Steven G. James made the announcement.

item.title: U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of New Mexico Weekly Immigration and Border Crimes Report
item.description: Today, the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Mexico announced its immigration enforcement statistics.

item.title: Haitian National Found Guilty of Conspiring to Distribute Methamphetamine
item.description: Djosaha Azulphar a/k/a “T,” age 28, a Haitian national and lawful permanent resident of the United States, has been found guilty of distribution of controlled substances, conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute a controlled substance, and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance following a four-day jury trial in federal court in Syracuse last week.

item.title: Broome County Man Pleads Guilty to Sending Threats to Kill and Injure Federal Officials
item.description: Jeffrey Scott Hamm, Jr., age 33, of Binghamton, New York, pleaded guilty Wednesday, September 16, 2026, to transmitting threats to injure another in interstate commerce.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement.

item.title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Marks Domestic Violence Awareness Month, Highlights Federal Funding for New Mexico Victim Services
item.description: The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Mexico joins the Department of Justice, the Office on Violence Against Women and communities across New Mexico in recognizing October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month and reaffirming its commitment to protecting victims, holding offenders accountable and supporting the organizations that serve survivors.

item.title: District Man Sentenced to 20-Year Prison Term for Killing Man in Southeast
item.description: Kenneth Coleman, 37, of Washington, D.C., was sentenced today to 240 months in prison for the murder of 24-year-old Jireh Martinez in November 2023, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

item.title: Apprehended Venezuelan Tren de Aragua Leader on FBI’s 10 Most Wanted Fugitives List Appears in Nebraska Court Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
item.description: The Justice Department announced the apprehension of Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre also known as “Prometheus” and “The Engineer,” 50, of Venezuela. Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre was added to the FBI’s “Top 10 Most Wanted Fugitives” list in March of 2026. Canelon Aguirre was the first cyber criminal and the 540th individual to be added to the Top 10 Most Wanted Fugitives list.
